title: When Is a Reasoning Model Worth Its API Cost?
description: A practical test for reasoning models: measure correct outcomes, token use and retries on your own tasks.
tldr: Compare models on cost per successful task, not headline token price alone. Reasoning models can consume extra output tokens; they are worth paying for when the improvement in correct outcomes exceeds that added cost.

sections.heading: Reasoning usage is easy to miss
sections.body: Some reasoning models spend tokens on internal reasoning as well as the visible answer. Provider usage accounting and output limits differ. Inspect the output or reasoning fields in actual responses, then price the billable usage according to the provider's current documentation.

sections.heading: Build a representative test set
sections.body: Collect 30–100 real tasks with clear success criteria. Include ordinary cases and costly failures. Run each candidate model with the same instructions and relevant settings. For each result, log total billable cost, correctness, latency and whether a retry or human correction was required.

sections.heading: Calculate cost per successful task
sections.body: If model A costs $0.01 per attempt and succeeds 70% of the time, its simple cost per success is about $0.0143. If model B costs $0.03 and succeeds 95%, its cost per success is about $0.0316. B costs more per successful result, but it may still win if errors create meaningful review or business costs. This is an illustrative calculation, not a benchmark claim.

sections.heading: Route selectively
sections.body: Many teams can use a cheaper model first and escalate only uncertain or high-stakes requests. Define an objective escalation rule and measure the added requests. A model choice is strongest when it is based on your tasks, quality threshold and observed token mix rather than a public leaderboard rank.

sections.heading: Use the tool for the price side
sections.body: [Tokens to USD](/tools/token-to-usd) converts measured input and output to a base text cost. Add reasoning, cache, tool or tier charges if the provider bills them separately. Then compare the complete cost with your quality results.

faq.question: Are reasoning tokens included in output cost?
faq.answer: Provider accounting varies. Check the API usage object and pricing documentation for your exact model; do not double-count a reasoning field already included in output usage.
